To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce BSMGs to model uncertainty over adversary types and MTD, and show how to use them to learn optimal movement strategies for MTD systems.

(i) we introduce the first unifying model of incomplete information in MTD that can capture the nuances of an attack-defense scenario and (ii) propose a learning algorithm for this model that converges to an equilibrium and outperforms the state-of-the art in MTD.

we propose a game-theoretic framework, called BSMG, to model MTD systems with uncertainty over the adversary type and a Bayesian learning approach that can learn the optimal defense policy in a reasonable time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How do we model MTD as leaderfollower games with incomplete information about attacker types? How do we learn movement strategies in such games? How do we evaluate the learned strategies?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new game model that captures the essence of the MTD system and an approach to learn optimal movement strategies in the presence of uncertainty about the adversary's behavior.
our proposed approach, BSS-Q, can learn optimal movement strategies in MTD domains even when there is incomplete knowledge about the adversary and the environment.

we propose a new model and learning approach for MTD, that can be used to learn movement strategies that can be applied to a wide range of domains and that is scalable and converges to an equilibrium in a reasonable time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel framework for modeling MTD as a Stackelberg Markow game with incomplete information, and propose a novel learning algorithm to solve such games in a scalable manner.
we have developed a novel game-theoretic framework for modeling MTD and proposed a learning approach for finding optimal movement strategies in such settings.
BSS-Q can learn the optimal policy for MTD systems with incomplete information and can be used to find good movement policies in MTD domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while learning movement strategies for moving target defense is a hard problem, the use of Bayesian Stackelberg Q learning can help us find good solutions in a reasonable time.
a Bayesian learning approach is essential for learning good movement strategies for MTD systems.

the strategic nature of an adversary cannot be ignored in sequential settings with uncertainty and the learning approach proposed in this work provides a way forward in designing scalable movement strategies for MTD.
